title: One fault a year (I.11)
hook: a resolution list, every item starting Monday, lost by spring: chapter eleven's arithmetic is one fault a year
tomorrow: why is it easier to stop a knock than a guest already inside?

segments.voice: A week inside a small book. Feel, not define. Unknown. Truth itself teaches. Weigh it. Truth, not style. And yesterday, chapter nine's safer road: under direction.
screen: `FEEL, NOT DEFINE · UNKNOWN · TRUTH ITSELF TEACHES.` → `WEIGH IT · TRUTH, NOT STYLE.` → `UNDER DIRECTION.`

segments.voice: January. A fresh note on the phone: run more, read more, sleep more, scroll less, call grandma, learn guitar. Every item starting Monday. By spring the note is buried under grocery lists. Chapter eleven of The Imitation of Christ has a different plan, and it's almost suspiciously small. If every year we rooted out one vice, it says, we would soon be perfect. One. Not the whole list. Then the chapter admits why even one is hard.
screen: `EVERY ITEM STARTING MONDAY.` → `BURIED BY SPRING.` → `ONE VICE A YEAR.`

segments.voice: Here's the honest part. Often, the chapter says, it goes the other way: people were better and purer at the start of their conversion than after many years. Fervor should grow every day; instead, it seems a great thing to keep even part of the first fire. And its fix is about timing. If we pushed against ourselves a little at the beginning, it says, we could afterward do everything with ease and joy. It's hard to give up what you're used to. But if you don't overcome small, easy things, how will you overcome the hard ones? So pick one, and lean hardest at the start. That's this week, too. Feel the sting instead of defining it. Do the good no one sees. Let truth teach you firsthand. Weigh the rumor. Seek the plain truth. Take the counsel. Six lines, and chapter eleven's quiet suggestion: don't try all six by Monday. One a year.
screen: `BETTER AT THE START THAN YEARS LATER.` · `PUSH HARDEST AT THE BEGINNING.` · `SMALL THINGS FIRST.` · `SIX LINES, ONE AT A TIME.` · then, large: `ONE A YEAR.`

segments.voice: Name one fault, just one, you'd like gone by this time next year. Picture the moment it usually shows up, and decide the one small thing you'll do in that moment instead. Then rest, with the plan made.
One fault a year. Chapter eleven's slow arithmetic: root out one vice at a time, pushing hardest at the start.
Hold on to this: one a year, slower than any resolution list, and meant to last. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1470 COUNTS.` → `THE IMITATION · 9 OF 30.` → `TOMORROW: WHY IS IT EASIER TO STOP A KNOCK THAN A GUEST ALREADY INSIDE?`
